candidate_relations.reason: Basal cell carcinoma with clear-cell features is a different tumor; prior nodular BCC is historical and this glans lesion is an infiltrative clear-cell neoplasm.
Metastatic clear-cell carcinoma was an explicit initial differential, not sebaceous carcinoma.
Clear-cell squamous cell carcinoma was the other initial differential and is not sebaceous carcinoma.
Malignant adnexal neoplasm is the correct parent family of sebaceous carcinoma but lacks sebaceous lineage.
Metastatic carcinoma is a competing explanation for a clear-cell penile mass, not the primary sebaceous carcinoma.
Clear-cell carcinoma of the penis is a descriptive parent and does not specify sebaceous carcinoma.
The truncated 'Metastatic clear' label points to metastatic clear-cell carcinoma, a differential rather than sebaceous carcinoma.
Adenocarcinoma is a broad parent that can include sebaceous carcinoma but omits the required sebaceous diagnosis.
Primary clear cell carcinoma of the penis remains a nonspecific clear-cell tumor and is not sebaceous carcinoma.
Clear cell squamous cell carcinoma of the penis is a related cutaneous differential with incompatible squamous rather than sebaceous lineage.
Balloon cell melanoma is a different clear-cell malignancy, not sebaceous carcinoma.
Metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma is a different primary and was only a differential.
